questions.q: An array has 5 elements. Which indexes are valid?
questions.e: Indexes start at 0, so an array of size n uses 0 to n − 1.

questions.q: What should the largest-value tracker start at?
questions.e: Start with a real element. If every value is negative, starting at 0 (or −1) would give a wrong answer.
The largest value 9 appears at indexes 2 and 4. With > the champion changes only on a strictly bigger value, so the first one (index 2) is kept.

questions.q: You need the first position of x. When should the loop stop?
o: At the first match, with break
When x is larger than a[i]
questions.e: Break at the first match, or a later match would overwrite the position. To count matches instead, never break.

questions.q: What happens if you read a[n] from an array of size n?
o: Out of bounds: garbage values or a crash
questions.e: C++ doesn't check the index. Reading past the end is undefined behaviour: wrong values, or a crash.
The run resets to 0 at the 0, so the longest run of 1s is the last three.

questions.q: The array's size comes from the input. What should you use?
questions.e: A vector's size can be decided while the program runs. Plain arrays need a constant size.
